correctness.rationale: Let a_j=b^j+c with integers b>=2,c>=−1. Each support diagonal is a matching. Union of first two matchings contains no alternating cycle because a two-step left-vertex move shifts by a fixed signed gap b−1. If c<b(b−2), for j>=1, a_(j+1)−2a_j=(b−2)b^j−c>0; every new matching edge has at most one previously incident endpoint, so attaching it cannot create a cycle. A finite cycle would be contained in a finite prefix. If c>=b(b−2), with q=b−1, a=c+1, the b+1 left vertices iq, b right vertices a−iq (i<b), and the final right vertex a+q are distinct and nonnegative, and four specified edge families assemble a 2(b+1)-cycle on first three support levels. At equality nonnegativity holds exactly, so cutoff is sharp. Published Theorem E of Zeng–Xue–Zeng transfers forestness to Abelian pattern Sturmian characteristic words. Independently checked 435 (b,c) pairs using exact union-find on first four support diagonals, bases 2..11 and offsets around thresholds; these checks are not the universal proof.

evidence: Strict-doubling sufficient condition implies a simple subrange, but (b,c)=(3,2) is a forest although strict doubling fails at the first support level. The envelope gives d_j>=2^j−1, a necessary global restriction; it cannot force a cycle at each forbidden c.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither stronger-looking sufficient growth nor necessary logarithmic density bounds imply the exact if-and-only-if threshold.
